name: New Topographics
summary: Flat, neutral, frontal views of suburbs, car parks and industrial sites, with no drama and no opinion. It shows the built landscape as a catalogue of facts, in a cool, exact, almost clerical style.

philosophy.core_thesis: The ordinary, man-made landscape deserves the formal care that the sublime wilderness once received, and the photographer's voice should stay out of it.
design_principles: Shoot frontally from a fixed height of 1.5m with the camera level, so that verticals stay parallel.
Wait for flat overcast or hazy light at a ratio of 2:1 or less, so that no shadow leads the eye.
Stand 10 to 50m from the subject, and fill 60% of the frame with ordinary built structure.
Use a view camera at f/22 to f/45 so that everything from the kerb to the horizon is sharp.
Keep the tonal scale narrow and neutral: black point at 5%, white point at 95%, with no toning.
Treat the subject as a type: photograph the same kind of object in a series, from the same distance and angle.
anti_patterns: Dramatic skies, golden hour and sunset colour
Picturesque framing that prettifies a car park or a tract house
Human emotion or an ironic gesture inside the frame
Heavy burning and dodging that adds mood

composition.framing: A calm, horizontal 4×5 or 8×10 frame; the subject sits in the middle band and the sky takes under 30%.
composition.viewpoint: Frontal, at 1.5m height, 10 to 50m from the subject, with level verticals.
composition.geometry: Orthogonal grids of houses, signs, lots and wires; the horizon runs at the same height in each picture of a series.
composition.subject_placement: Centred or evenly balanced; no subject is the hero, so the eye scans the whole frame.

light.quality: Flat and shadowless: overcast, haze or open shade.
light.direction: From everywhere; if the sun is out, it comes from behind the camera and does not draw a shadow edge.
light.time_of_day: Overcast day, or late morning haze

lens_and_camera.format: 4×5 in or 8×10 in view camera; 6×7 medium format as a modern equivalent
lens_and_camera.focus: Set the plane of sharp focus with a little front tilt to cover the kerb to the horizon.

colour_and_grade.treatment: Neutral black and white with a narrow, even scale, or restrained, desaturated colour; no tone.
grade_recipe: Convert to monochrome with a neutral mix (R 33, G 33, B 33).
Set the black point at 5% and the white point at 95%.
Keep midtone contrast flat: a straight curve, with −10% contrast.
Match the exposure of each picture in a series to within 0.3 stop.
Apply no dodging, burning, vignette or tone.
colour_and_grade.grain: ISO 100 fine grain; not visible at 20 × 25 cm

subject_and_staging.staging: None; the photographer chooses a spot and a time, and records the site as it is.
subject_and_staging.direction: No people, or people small and incidental; no pose.

workflow: Develop normally and print on a neutral paper, grade 2.
Print each series to the same density and the same size.
Hang as a set in even rows of 20 to 40 pictures.
Add a plain caption of place and date.
post_processing.output: A small, quiet, grey print, about 20 × 25 cm, in a series with a plain caption.

canonical_works.work: The New Industrial Parks near Irvine, California
New Topographics: Photographs of a Man-Altered Landscape

emotion.target_response: Cool attention: the viewer feels the plainness of a place and starts to read it, not to feel about it.

avoid_when: The brief wants drama, glamour or emotional warmth.
The subject is a person and not a place.

modifiers.how: Switch to colour negative film at ISO 100; keep the frontal view, the level horizon and the flat light, and let the colour of signs and paint in.
Wait for side light at 4:1, widen the tonal scale to a true black and white, and keep the large format and the f/45 aperture.

sources.title: Wikidata Q76188811: New Topographics: Photographs of a Man-Altered Landscape (SFMOMA 2010 exhibition)
William Jenkins, New Topographics: Photographs of a Man-Altered Landscape (George Eastman House, 1975)
